Subject: Prod sizing request: long-context retrieval + chat bursts

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re ready to scope a Dedicated pool for CloudScale’s production workload and I wanted to share a compact summary of the traffic profile so your team can recommend a sizing plan and any recommended quantization tradeoffs.

Workload summary (target prod):
- Concurrent active users: 1,200 (peak hour)
- Two primary features:
  1) Contextual retrieval + long answer generation (80k token context, ~6–12 generated tokens per user request on average) — accounts for ~18% of requests but high memory.
  2) Short chat / UI assistants (2k context, 16 tokens generated) — ~70% of requests, latency-sensitive.
- Expected qps (aggregate peak): 350 qps
- Prefix reuse: many sessions reuse the same retrieval window for repeated queries (~65% reuse on long-context flows).
- Models considered: "rw-70b" family (we want headroom for an eventual 100k context variant) and a smaller 13b conv model for chat.

We attached a small traffic sample and would like:
1) GPU fleet recommendation (count + instance type mix) for initial Dedicated commit.
2) Suggested quantization profiles per model (and expected perf/memory delta).
3) Any operational mitigations (KV caching, offloading, sharding) we should plan for.

Can you loop in your infra/SE folks? We’re hoping to finalize capacity and cost in the next two weeks.

Thanks,
Sophie
Sophie Tran
Head of Platform Engineering, CloudScale AI

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Prod sizing request: long-context retrieval + chat bursts

Folks —

I ran an initial capacity model against the CloudScale sample. Below are assumptions and per-GPU estimates so the sales side has numbers to share. I kept the math conservative and separated the two workload types.

Assumptions (conservative):
- "rw-70b" dense weights un-quantized (FP16) ~ 35–40 GB resident on GPU memory (model-only).
- Int8 quant reduces model footprint ~45–55% vs FP16; int4 reduces further but may need kernel/runtime flags and has some perf variance.
- KV cache: estimated per-token cost depends on hidden size; for rw-70b we estimate ~300–380 bytes per token in FP16 (includes keys+values + intermediate alignment). Int8/int4 cache representations reduce that footprint by ~1.7–2.2x depending on implementation and whether we keep some tensors in FP16 for compute.
- Prefix reuse: CloudScale reports ~65% reuse for long-context — caching will reduce repeated decoding cost but not the initial KV allocation.

Short-chat (2k context) — target latency p95 ~200–350ms:
- Model: 13B conv for chat (13B FP16 model ~12–14 GB).
- KV per short session: 2k tokens x ~120 bytes/token ~ 240MB (FP16). With int8, ~120–150MB.
- Concurrency per 80GB H100 (p95 target): ~80–110 concurrent short-chat sessions (depends on batch packing). For L40s / A10s (48GB) expect ~35–50 sessions.

Long-context (80k) — heavy memory footprint:
- Model weight residency: rw-70b FP16 ~35–40 GB; int8 quant -> ~18–22 GB; int4 -> ~10–12 GB (requires optimized kernels).
- KV cache for 80k context (FP16 estimate): 80k tokens x 320 bytes/token -> ~25.6 GB. Using int8 KV representation reduces to ~11–13 GB; int4 down to ~6–7 GB (but int4 generally requires a mixed-precision runtime path).
- Effective per-session GPU memory (model + kv + headroom) -> FP16: ~66–70 GB (70B + 80k KV) — fits only on 80GB class GPUs with very little headroom; int8 path -> ~32–36 GB; int4 path -> ~17–22 GB.
- Concurrency per H100 80GB (70B)
  - FP16 path: ~1 concurrent long-context session (practically none for steady-state).
  - Int8 path: ~2–4 concurrent sessions (depends on runtime fragmentation and activations).
  - Int4 path (optimized): ~6–10 concurrent sessions.

Operational suggestions:
1) Hybrid fleet: start with a mixed pool of H100 80GB (for FP16 canary and worst-case failover) + L40s (48GB) or A100s for chat-heavy nodes. Long-context heavy traffic should route to an int8/int4-optimized pool.
2) KV caching strategy: aggressively cache retrieval windows and pre-warm common prefixes. Because CloudScale has ~65% prefix reuse, effective memory amortization reduces service-level tco by ~25–40% at peak.
3) Fallback model variants: expose a 100k-context offload path that converts long sessions to archive + sparse context (for requests older than X minutes) to free KV memory.
4) Canary rollout: begin with int8 quantized endpoints for long-context (validate quality on holdout prompts), then incrementally enable int4 for traffic slices with golden prompts.
5) Autoscaling knobs: maintain a low-latency short-chat pool with horizontal autoscaling by qps; long-context workers should scale on active session counts (not qps) because memory dominates.

Sizing snapshot (initial commit recommendation) — conservative starting point:
- Pool A (chat-heavy, 2k contexts): 6 x L40s (48GB) — expected peak capacity ~300–350 short-chat concurrent sessions across the pool.
- Pool B (long-context production): 8 x H100 80GB with int8 runtime (can be used in int4 later) — expected concurrent long-context session capacity ~20–30 (est. 2–4 per GPU). This covers initial long-context demands with headroom.
- Reserve 2 x H100 as overflow/emergency for FP16-only workloads and migration testing.

Cost vs performance tradeoff guidance:
- Int8 gives ~2x memory reduction and modest CPU/GPU perf gains — recommended as the production default after validation.
- Int4 unlocks the largest density, but expect more tuning (kernel stability, slight quality drift on some prompts). Use progressive rollout.

I’ll attach a short workbook with per-GPU math (sheets: assumptions / per-model footprints / sizing scenarios). Rishi — can you confirm the latency assumptions and whether we should conservatively price 25% more headroom for fragmentation?

- Marcus
Senior Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Marcus — math looks good to me. A few additions from SE/readout perspective before we lock the commit: 

1) Latency verification plan:
- Short-chat (2k): run a 48-hour soak with L40s using a representative mix: 70% short-chat, 18% long-context stubs, 12% control traffic. Aim for p95 < 350ms.
- Long-context: validate p99 quantiles for generation tail latency on int8 path. If p99s exceed SLA, we’ll shift a portion of long-context reads to backgrounded jobs and stream partial responses.

2) Quality gating for quantization:
- We’ll run an automated eval suite (1000 golden prompts) comparing FP16 vs int8 vs int4 on relevance and hallucination metrics. If int8 deviates <1.5% on combined score, we greenlight; int4 needs manual spot checks.

3) Deployment / rollout plan:
- Phase 0: Canary int8 on 10% of long-context traffic on Pool B.
- Phase 1: Gradual 10% increments over 7 days with eval and rollback hooks.
- Phase 2: Enable int4 on a small customer-facing cohort after two weeks of stable metrics.

4) Mutual action plan (high level):
- Week 0: Sign Dedicated commit (capacity ranges A & B) and exchange procurement contacts.
- Week 1–2: Provision reserved instances + run 48-hour load tests.
- Week 3: Canary int8 rollout; automated evaluation runs.
- Week 4: Full production cutover for long-context to int8 path + monitoring.

Sophie — if this sequencing works, we’ll add the formal timelines to the workbook and a suggested MOP.

- Rishi
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
